correctness.rationale: Poisson summation of the explicit difference of Cauchy-kernel Fourier transforms yields hyperbolic K_lambda. For sin(theta) nonzero, simultaneous vanishing of two real components violates strict monotonicity of a cosh ratio except at xi=1/2, where the common component is strictly decreasing. For theta=0 and pi, strict sinh/cosh quotient monotonicity gives only theta=0,xi=1/2. At xi=0 the signed zero-frequency convention cancels in the difference, leaving a nonzero multiple of sin(theta). The coincident-pole limit is a derivative of K_lambda and strict derivative signs give the identical zero set. At each of three zeros, real and imaginary directional derivatives are both nonzero, so the Jacobian is invertible. A standalone checker verified direct Zak series against both distinct-pole and repeated-pole formulas; finite grid testing is supplementary only.

value.rationale: Parity alone produces at least three Zak zeros for odd windows, whereas hidden zeros may create additional periodic Gabor obstructions. This theorem eliminates all such hidden zeros for every member of a naturally parametrized sign-changing rational two-imaginary-pole-pair family, proves the three zeros are stable and transverse, and includes the nontrivial repeated-pole boundary. That exact structural classification is a motivated invariant, not a routine restatement of parity or a numerical sample.
